::: {.lead}
It is Monday morning at Sunrise Company, a small company with an office and
a shop. Mona, the office assistant, has six jobs before 11:00. With the right
app, each job takes minutes. By hand, the same jobs take her all day. In this
lesson you learn which apps help people at study and at work. You also meet a
new kind of app: the AI assistant. These notes are a short reference: in
class you try each idea on the computer, as an experiment of the
**worksheet**.
:::

## Key terms

{{< glossary digital-skills productivity office-suite word-processor spreadsheet presentation-app cloud-storage ai-assistant generative-ai prompt >}}

## 1.1 Why every job needs digital skills

Look at job adverts today. A shop wants "Excel and e-mail". A bank wants
"Microsoft Office". An office wants "Word, Excel and AI tools". Almost every
job uses a computer or a phone (@fig-jobs).

![Every job uses digital tools.](images/jobs.png){#fig-jobs width=92%}

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 1.1 — Digital skills"}
**Digital skills** are what you can do with a computer, a phone and apps.
For example, you write a letter, add up prices or send a file.
:::

Good apps save time. We call this **productivity**: you finish more useful
work in less time. A computer does the simple, repeated work. You plan the
work and check the result.

::: {.callout-note title="Example 1.1 — Eight prices"}
Mona needs the total of 8 prices: 12, 25, 8, 40, 15, 30, 5 and 20 JD.

1. By hand, she adds the prices one by one. It takes about 30 seconds.
2. In a spreadsheet, she presses **AutoSum**. The total, 155 JD, appears at
   once.
3. Then one price changes from 8 to 18 JD. By hand, she adds everything
   again. The spreadsheet shows the new total, 165 JD, by itself.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/time-saver.html" poster="sims/time-saver.png" title="Time Saver: by hand or with an app?" height="620" >}}

*In class: Experiment 1 of the worksheet, eight prices by hand and with AutoSum.*

## 1.2 The main productivity apps

Most offices use an **office suite**. This is a set of apps that work
together. The most common one is **Microsoft 365**. Google Workspace has the
same kinds of apps. Your university account opens Microsoft 365 in the lab
and in the browser.

Each app has one main job (@fig-apps):

![The main productivity apps and their jobs.](images/app-types.png){#fig-apps width=100%}

| App | Kind of app | Main job |
|---|---|---|
| Word | word processor | letters, reports, CVs |
| Excel | spreadsheet | numbers, lists, totals, charts |
| PowerPoint | presentation app | slides for a talk |
| Outlook | e-mail and calendar | messages, files to send, meetings |
| OneDrive | cloud storage | your files on every device |
| Teams | chat and online meetings | talk to people who are far away |
| Copilot | AI assistant | ask in normal words; it writes and sums up |

: The apps of Microsoft 365 that you use in this course. {#tbl-apps}

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Students often make a table of numbers in Word and add the numbers by hand.
Use Excel for numbers: it calculates for you, and it does not make
mistakes in sums.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/app-launcher.html" poster="sims/app-launcher.png" title="App Launcher: which app for the job?" height="640" >}}

*In class: Experiment 2 of the worksheet, the apps of Microsoft 365 and their jobs.*

## 1.3 AI assistants: a new kind of app

Mona gets a long e-mail from an angry customer. She needs a short, polite
reply. Today she can ask an **AI assistant** for help. An AI assistant is an
app that you ask in normal words. Examples are Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT and
Gemini.

These apps use **generative AI**: they make new text or pictures from your
request. Your request is called a **prompt** (@fig-ai).

![An AI assistant: you ask, it writes, you check.](images/ai-assistant.png){#fig-ai width=100%}

AI assistants are good at some jobs:

- a first draft of an e-mail or a letter;
- a summary of a long text;
- ideas, for example for a poster;
- a translation of a short text.

But AI makes mistakes. It can write a wrong fact or a wrong number. It
sounds sure, even when it is wrong. So **you check every answer**, and you
are responsible for what you use.

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 1.2 — The AI rule of this course"}
Use AI for drafts and ideas. Check every fact and number. Never type
personal data (an ID number, a card number, a phone number) into an AI tool.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Example 1.2 — Three prompts"}
Mona wants to ask an AI assistant three things.

1. "Sum up this long customer e-mail in 3 points." A good job for AI. Mona
   reads the e-mail too.
2. "When did Sunrise Company open its first shop?" The AI does not know a
   small company. It may invent a date. Mona checks a real source.
3. "Fill in this bank form. My ID number is …" No! This is personal data.
   Mona fills in the form herself.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/ai-chat.html" poster="sims/ai-chat.png" title="AI Chat: is this a good job for an AI assistant?" height="640" >}}

*In class: Experiment 3 of the worksheet, a first prompt and a check of the answer.*

## Case study: Monday at Sunrise Company

Mona works from 9:00 to 11:00 on six jobs. Without AI, with the right apps,
the jobs take 120 minutes: she finishes at 11:00. An AI assistant can make
three jobs faster: the e-mails (20 → 10 minutes), the slides (30 → 20) and
the report (40 → 25). Then she finishes at 10:25.

| Job | App | AI help? |
|---|---|---|
| Reply to 3 e-mails from customers | Outlook | yes: first drafts |
| Add up the 30 sales of the week | Excel | no: Excel adds exactly |
| Make 5 slides about new products | PowerPoint | yes: an outline |
| Write a one-page report for the manager | Word | yes: a first draft, then check |
| Clean the customer list (names and phone numbers) | Excel | no: personal data |
| Share the report with the manager | OneDrive | no: AI cannot share files |

: Mona's Monday: the right app and the right use of AI. {#tbl-monday}

## Further reading

Evans, Martin and Poatsy, *Technology in Action*, 18th ed., the chapters on
application software and on artificial intelligence.

## Exercises

1. What are digital skills? Give two examples.
2. What is productivity? Explain it with one example.
3. Which app do you use for each job: a CV, a chart of sales, a talk with
   slides?
4. What is an office suite? Name one.
5. What does cloud storage give you?
6. What is a prompt? Write one prompt for a short summary.
7. Write two jobs that an AI assistant does well.
8. Why must you check the answer of an AI assistant?
9. Ali types his phone number and his ID number into an AI tool. What is the
   mistake?
10. Mona uses AI for the e-mails, the slides and the report. How many minutes
    does she save (10 + 10 + 15)?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. What you can do with a computer, a phone and apps; for example, write a letter and add up prices.
2. More useful work in less time; for example, AutoSum adds 8 prices at once.
3. Word; Excel; PowerPoint.
4. A set of office apps that work together; Microsoft 365 (or Google Workspace).
5. Your files on the Internet; you open them on every device.
6. The request that you type to an AI assistant; for example, "Sum up this text in 3 points."
7. For example: first drafts, summaries, ideas, translations.
8. AI can write wrong facts and numbers, and it sounds sure.
9. He gave personal data to an AI tool; never type personal data.
10. 35 minutes.
:::
